how: Same world, same seed, changed only the training objective.
interpretation: Plain reading: a penalty on variance alone lets the network copy one useful direction into all 8 outputs; a penalty on correlation between outputs prevents that. This is a training-recipe fix, not a change to what counts as success.

what: Stage A main result: the model cleanly separated the slow hidden numbers from the fast ones, on all 5 seeds.

interpretation: These runs are supposed to fail. They did, so the main-arm success is attributable to the pairing information and to prediction, not an accident of the setup.

how: Old bound: slow-block R2 below 0.5. But picking 4 of 8 directions at random already explains about half the variance, so shuffled runs legitimately scored 0.31-0.54. New bound: recovered angle above 45 degrees (observed 73-88). The plan's own expectation (gap flattens) held throughout.
interpretation: Disclosed because it was decided after seeing data. It affects only a control, not the pass criteria.

interpretation: Shows where this simple recipe starts to fail. It matches the direction the authors report. Plan criteria apply at strength 0.5; the sweep maps the limit. Stage B should be run at 0.5 first.

interpretation: The fix is empirically supported; the explanation is untested. Do not cite 'rank collapse' as established in any write-up unless a rank check is added.
what: CORRECTION to entry #5 (and to my earlier chat summary): I said the first failure was the network collapsing onto a single direction. That mechanism was not measured. What was measured: without the correlation penalty the run fails (slow-block R2 0.43, 7 of 8 output directions still active); with it, it works (R2 0.99). Why the penalty helps is a hypothesis, not a finding.

plain.did: Ran the runs that should fail, to make sure the pass means something.
output: Shuffled matched pairs: gap ratio 1.00-1.02 (vs about 94 for the real run). Split destroyed.
No spectral head (the paper's LeJEPA baseline): invariant_r2 0.486 ± 0.080, block_purity 0.488 ± 0.082, global_r2 unchanged (0.989 ± 0.003).
Paper's LeJEPA gets about 0.96 block R² here, much higher than our 0.49. Likely cause: their encoder is built to mirror the scrambling function. Not tested.
No prediction: invariant_r2 0.21-0.46.
No variance regularizer / no ZCA: invariant_r2 0.01-0.14.
plain.relevance: Each ingredient (prediction, matched pairs, whitening) is needed. Our result isn't an accident of the setup. The global_r2 staying the same without the spectral head matches the paper: the head separates the blocks, it does not change how much the representation holds.
